CVX.rationale: Chevron's fundamental health is solid but deteriorating: Q1 2026 showed $48.61B revenue (+2.1% YoY) but EPS collapsed 44.5% YoY to $1.11, driven by $3B in unfavorable timing effects on derivatives and a downstream loss of $817M. Operating cash flow fell sharply to $2.51B from $5.19B a year ago. However, upstream earnings grew 4% YoY to $3.9B, production guidance of 7-10% growth is intact, and management reaffirmed $3-4B structural cost reduction target by year-end 2026. The balance sheet remains strong with $189B equity and a low net-debt-to-capital ratio. The integrated model provides natural hedges, and the company maintains its 39-year dividend streak at $1.78/quarter with $2.5B in Q1 buybacks. Valuation is stretched: P/E of 32.9x is at the top of its 365-day range (15.1-32.9x), more than double the 15.86x level from May 2025, while net margin has compressed from 7.8% to 5.9% and ROE from 10.5% to 5.9%. The stock has rallied ~20% since November 2025, largely pricing in the oil price surge from the Iran/Strait of Hormuz conflict (WTI at $104.66). Near-term catalysts include potential $1B timing effect unwind in Q2 and elevated oil prices supporting cash flow, but these are partially offset by climate litigation reserves ($350-400M), California regulatory scrutiny on refining margins, and the risk that oil prices normalize. The combination of deteriorating earnings quality, stretched valuation vs history, and geopolitical tailwinds that may prove temporary yields a mildly positive but cautious view.
